title: Welcome to Module 2: Pub/Sub & Content Filtering 📡
content: AMPS is a low-latency messaging system at its core.
Today we explore how AMPS routes data efficiently.
speakerNotes: Welcome students! In this module, we'll dive into the heart of AMPS messaging: how to define topics and filter content for maximum efficiency.

title: Ad Hoc Topics: Zero Configuration ⚡
content: AMPS does not require pre-declaring topics for basic Pub/Sub.
**Ad Hoc Topics:** Topics created 'on the fly' when a publisher sends data.
Publishers and subscribers are completely decoupled.
A topic name determines the message stream.
speakerNotes: One of AMPS' strengths is that you don't need to configure topics in advance for simple messaging. This is what we call 'Ad Hoc Topics'.

title: Topic Identifiers 🏷️
content: Topics are the primary way to categorize message streams.
**Regex Subscriptions:** Subscribers can use regular expressions to match multiple topics.
speakerNotes: Subscribers can use regular expressions to listen to multiple topics at once, further decoupling them from the publisher's specific topic choices.

title: Content Filtering: The 'WHERE' Clause 🔍
content: Content Filtering allows subscribers to receive only the data they need.
- **Bandwidth Efficiency:** Less data sent over the wire.
- **Decoupling:** Publishers don't need to know subscriber needs.
- **Simpler Clients:** Code only processes relevant messages.
speakerNotes: Think of content filtering as a SQL WHERE clause for your message stream. It moves the selection logic from the client to the server.

title: Message Routing Logic 🛤️
content: AMPS evaluates content filters for every message published.
mermaid:
graph TD
  Pub[Publisher] -- Message --> AMPS{AMPS Server}
  AMPS -- "Filter: /Sym='IBM'" --> Sub1[Subscriber 1]
  AMPS -- "Filter: /Price > 100" --> Sub2[Subscriber 2]
  AMPS -- "No Filter" --> Sub3[Subscriber 3]
  style AMPS fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px
speakerNotes: This diagram shows how AMPS acts as a high-speed router, evaluating filters to determine which subscribers should receive a particular message.

title: AMPS Filter Grammar 🏗️
content: AMPS uses a combination of two standards:
1. **XPath Identifiers:** To locate fields within the message.
2. **SQL-92 Operators:** To form the comparison predicate.
speakerNotes: If you know XPath and SQL, you already know 90% of AMPS filtering. We use XPath for paths and SQL for the logic.

title: XPath Identifiers in AMPS 📍
content: Identifiers specify the value of an attribute or element.
- **Special Names:** `[/Field With Spaces]` (use brackets for non-standard names).
speakerNotes: AMPS uses a subset of XPath. For FIX, we use the tag number as the field name. Brackets allow for field names that don't fit standard XPath naming rules.

title: AMPS Data Types 💎
content: AMPS is 'transparently typed'. It converts as needed.
speakerNotes: AMPS tries to be helpful. If you compare a string '100' to a number 50, it will attempt to convert the string to a number for the comparison.

title: Logical & Arithmetic Operators ➕
content: ⚠️ **Tip:** Use spaces around `/` in arithmetic to avoid XPath confusion (e.g., `/qty / 10` vs `/qty/10`).
speakerNotes: Standard precedence applies. Always remember the space around the division operator to ensure the parser doesn't think it's part of an XPath identifier.

title: Comparison Operators ⚖️
speakerNotes: IN is highly optimized in AMPS. It's generally faster than using multiple OR statements for the same field.

title: String Operators: LIKE, BEGINS WITH 🧵
content: - **LIKE**: Full PCRE (Perl Compatible Regular Expression) matching.
speakerNotes: BEGINS WITH is a specialized, high-performance operator. Use LIKE when you need the full power of regular expressions.

title: Handling NULL & NaN 🧩
content: In AMPS, comparisons with `NULL` are never true.
speakerNotes: SQL semantics apply to NULL. You must use 'IS NULL' to check for existence, as `/field = NULL` will always be false.

title: Working with Arrays 📚
content: 1. **Comparisons (=, <, LIKE):** Evaluate every element. Returns true if *any* match.
speakerNotes: This is a powerful feature. Comparison operators check if any element in the array matches the condition.

title: Expression Optimization 🚀
content: - **Short-Circuiting:** In `A OR B`, B is only evaluated if A is false.
- **Partial Parsing:** AMPS only parses fields used in filters/indexes.
- **Hash Indexes:** Exact string matches on SOW topics are ultra-fast.
speakerNotes: To optimize your filters, put the least expensive or most likely to be true conditions on the left side of an OR statement.

title: Module 2 Summary 🏁
content: ✅ **Ad Hoc Topics:** No setup required for basic Pub/Sub.
✅ **Regex Topics:** Subscribe to many topics at once.
✅ **Content Filters:** Precise data delivery using XPath + SQL.
✅ **Strong Types:** Transparent conversion for ease of use.
✅ **Optimized:** Short-circuiting and partial parsing keep AMPS fast.
speakerNotes: We've covered the basics of how AMPS identifies topics and filters content. Next, we'll look at the State of the World (SOW) database.
